questions.question: Odontogenic infection.

parts.text: Name 2 bugs not covered by amox
Name 2 bugs not covered by metronidazole
Explain why metronidazole only covers anaerobe and not aerobe

cohort_answer.text: Bugs not covered by amox: Fusobacterium (some resistance to PCN, significant resistance to clindamycin and linezolid; susceptible to Flagyl, beta-lactam/beta-lactamase inhibitor combos and carbapenems); Prevotella (significant resistance to clindamycin; susceptible to Flagyl, beta-lactam/beta-lactamase inhibitor combos, carbapenems, linezolid); Porphyromonas (susceptible to Flagyl and beta-lactam/beta-lactamase inhibitor combos, carbapenems, linezolid; significant resistance to clindamycin); Peptostreptococcus. Bugs not covered by metronidazole: all the aerobes - Streptococcus, Moraxella, Lactobacillus, Enterobacteriaceae. Why metronidazole only covers anaerobes: the enzyme that activates/oxidizes metronidazole (pyruvate:ferredoxin oxidoreductase / ferredoxin) is only present in anaerobic bacteria, not aerobic ones.

questions.question: Odontogenic infection

parts.text: 2 relevant organisms not covered by amoxicillin
2 relevant organisms not covered by metronidazole
Why does metronidazole work against anaerobes but not aerobes?

questions.model_answer:
a) Two organisms not covered by amoxicillin: beta-lactamase-producing anaerobes (Prevotella/Fusobacterium species) and Staphylococcus aureus (beta-lactamase-producing/MRSA strains).
b) Two organisms not covered by metronidazole: viridans/anginosus group streptococci and Staphylococcus aureus (both facultative aerobes).
c) Metronidazole works against anaerobes because its nitro group is reduced only by low-redox-potential anaerobic electron transport enzymes (e.g., pyruvate-ferredoxin oxidoreductase), generating DNA-damaging free radicals; aerobic organisms lack this reductive pathway and thus cannot activate the drug, rendering it inactive against them.

parts.text: List FIVE antibiotics that have such excellent bioavailability that the oral formulation should always be used instead of the IV formulation.

questions.model_answer: 5 antibiotics with such excellent bioavailability that oral should be used instead of IV: (1) ciprofloxacin/levofloxacin (fluoroquinolones), (2) metronidazole, (3) linezolid, (4) doxycycline, (5) trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (fluconazole, though an antifungal, is another classic example if antifungals are permitted).

questions.question: A patient has an odontogenic infection:

parts.text: Name 2 bacteria not covered by metronidazole.
Name 2 bacteria not covered by amoxicillin.
Why does metronidazole not cover aerobes?

cohort_answer.text: a) Actinomyces; Propionibacterium acnes; Lactobacillus. b) H. flu (beta lactamase); Moraxella (beta lactamase); B. fragilis; Prevotella. c) Reductive activation only occurs in obligate anaerobes; reductive particles (nitrogen radicals) interact with DNA causing strand breakage and fatal destabilization of DNA helix.
